subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support controlling a regular Slack user identity through user-level Socket Mode events and xoxp writes, and if so under what explicit security/authorization guard?
rationale: The requested behavior changes Slack identity and token-selection semantics beyond the current documented bot-first Slack model, so a code worker should not decide the product/security boundary alone.

options.title: Approve explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a deliberate Slack user-identity mode with user-event authorization checks, xoxp reply routing, scopes/docs, and live Slack proof before implementation is considered done.

options.title: Keep bot-only inbound model
options.body: Document that user tokens remain supplemental read/fallback-write credentials and regular-user DM control is out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a deliberate Slack user-identity mode with user-event authorization checks, xoxp reply routing, scopes/docs, and live Slack proof before implementation is considered done.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows work on the affected Slack token, routing, and reply surfaces, making this the best available routing candidate for the product/security decision.
